defs_parts: Six labels sit in the corners of the pictures that follow.
In the book text: the course text uses and explains the term.
In the glossary: the term is on the course term list, but the text does not explain it.
Computed: the numbers are worked out on screen from stated inputs.
Simulation: a made-up run with a fixed seed, so it comes out the same every time.
Illustrative data: numbers chosen to show the idea, not measured.
Conceptual: a drawing of the idea, with no data behind it.
recap_lines: Scaling shrinks frequent errors, not the categorical limit at the sample's edge.
The system supplies symbols, the supervisor supplies meaning and directedness.
A wider sample still has a boundary, and the data-world gap sits there.
A validation set tests the system's question, not the world's.
Where the limits bite, the supervisor's doubt is the safeguard.
Only a person can carry accountability, so the sign-off is never delegated.
bookends.segment: Name The Limit, Defend The Term
bookends.command: Give me short deployment cases one at a time. For each, I must name the exact term that fits and say why its look-alike is wrong. Draw from these terms, data-world gap, categorical boundary, distribution shift, Extremistan, circular signal, fictitious override, stop condition, delegate and verify, and accountability. Hold back the answer until I reply, then correct my wording.
checks: Check: Each case can be answered with one exact term from the list.
Check: The answer stays hidden until you have replied.
